Name: item_value_consumer_decomposition
Title: Whose Value Is It? Decomposing Retrieved-Item Counterfactual Value into a Consumer-Invariant Procedure Part and a Consumer-Specific Residual
Short Hypothesis: The leave-one-out value of a retrieved experience item is the sum of a type-level part that the best static type-conditioned arm (static3: three fixed expert exemplars, +12.4 net over k=0 under Qwen3-32B) already carries and that transfers across readers, and an item-specific residual (the per-item composition of the measured +17.2 net that k=3 retrieval adds over static3) that is reliable within a reader but does not transfer. On identical retrieved sets: the disattenuated cross-reader rank agreement of item residuals is below 0.5 while within-reader split-half reliability is at least 0.5; the residual concentrates in item classes that invite verbatim copying (long-detour self-written trajectories) and costs a weaker reader more than a stronger one; value-guided item selection estimated under one reader is worthless under another; and the residual is a property of the backbone rather than of its current policy, so it survives self-distillation of the same reader but not a capability-matched reader of another family.
Related Work: Per-item value is measured by intervention only under one generator: CUE-R REMOVE/REPLACE (2604.05467), document Shapley (2507.04480), DIG confidence gain (2509.12765, which explicitly does not examine transfer across generators). Agent memory systems claim model-agnosticism at the system level: ExpGraph/ExpSuite (2605.30712) swaps frozen executors and ablates modules, ReMe (2512.10696) reports that a smaller model with memory beats a larger one without, and CHIME (2609.02074) evolves separate planning and execution banks with attribute-before-memorize; none asks whether the utility of an individual experience learned under executor A is its utility under executor B. In the home literature, training-data value is known to be model-dependent (Data Shapley 1904.02868; DataInf 2310.00902) and proxy-model transfer of data-curation decisions is unreliable (2512.24503; DataDecide 2504.11393 finds it works only for likelihood-type proxies); this idea imports that question to in-context retrieved items with an intervention ground truth and a decomposition. The program's own memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) asserted that item value is not an item property but had no intervention arm.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, and several claim the scores are model-agnostic, yet no per-item score has been re-measured under a second consumer. We ask whether the counterfactual value of a retrieved ALFWorld experience item belongs to the item or to the reader that consumes it. Holding the retrieved sets fixed (the logged rank-ordered ids from the k-sweep), we measure leave-one-out (REMOVE) and token-matched REPLACE effects of the same items under Qwen3-32B (reader A), Qwen3-8B (reader B: same family, weaker), gemma-3-27b-it (reader D: other family, capability-matched) and a self-distilled LoRA variant of Qwen3-32B (reader C: same backbone, shifted policy, the drift case of G16). Item value is decomposed against Measurement C's best static arm (static3, +12.4 over k=0; k=3 adds +17.2 over it under A): the type-level part is what static3 carries, the residual is the item's REMOVE effect with static3 present. Item classes are manufactured as with-arms at position 1 of the same natural set, so class comparisons are direct paired contrasts on the same (game, seed): planted wrong-procedure, cross-type token-matched placebo, short and long-detour self-written. Transfer is tested at matched noise by the disattenuated cross-reader Spearman of item residuals with a bootstrap CI on the ratio itself, and its operational consequence by cross-fitted, shrinkage-corrected value-guided top-3 selection estimated under one reader and deployed under another, paired game by game at 2,740 episodes per arm. Readers C and D separate a policy shift from a backbone swap at matched capability. The contribution is a statement of what a per-item score means when the reader changes: which component transfers, which does not, in which classes the non-transferable part lives, whether it is a backbone or a policy property, and at what re-run cost the residual can be estimated to a stable rank.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld, expert bank, bank-target partition as in the starting position; 274 valid games (seen+unseen); a cell is 274 games x S seeds of paired episodes with S chosen per arm (S=4: 1,096, +/-5.7; S=6: 1,644, +/-4.6; S=10: 2,740, +/-3.6, scaled from the measured +/-8 at 548). Retrieved sets are frozen to the logged rank-ordered ids (retrieval is by task-text similarity and does not depend on the reader), so the reader is the only manipulated variable. Static arm = static3 (Measurement C's best static arm: 3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached). Readers: A Qwen3-32B (GPU0), B Qwen3-8B (same family, weaker; GPU1), D gemma-3-27b-it (other family, capability-matched to A), C Qwen3-32B plus the program's self-distilled LoRA (same backbone, shifted policy). E0 (reported arm, not a gate): reader B k-sweep k in {0,1,3,7} on the logged sets at S=4 (k=3 at S=10 because it doubles as the similarity top-3 arm of E4); B's k3-k0 and k3-static3 are reported whatever they are, and every later arm runs under B regardless, so a reader that ignores item content is an outcome P1 records, not a screen. E1 ground truth per reader (A, B): REMOVE position 1 (S=6; also the shared without-arm of E3), REMOVE 2/3 (S=4), token-matched cross-type REPLACE at position 1 (S=4), k=1 vs k=0 as the second set composition (S=4), pairwise removal of all three pairs on 1 seed (822) for additivity, item-order shuffle on 1 seed (274); logged k-sweep and static3 arms under A are reused and topped up to the required S. E2 decomposition per reader (A, B): static3 (S=4), static3+k3 (S=6), static3+REMOVE 1/2/3 (S=6; 4,932 residual contrasts per reader); residual_i = success(static3+k3) minus success(static3+k3 without i) on the same (game, seed); procedural part of an item's type = static3 minus k0; per-item analysis on items with >= 8 residual contrasts (expected 150-250 items, each retrieved for >= 2 games and so with >= 12 contrasts at S=6). E3 manufactured classes, all as with-arms at position 1 of the natural k=3 set on the same (game, seed), so class comparisons are direct paired with-vs-with contrasts and never differences of two cells: C1 = natural same-type expert (the k=3 arm), C2 planted wrong-procedure (same-type expert trajectory with the procedure receptacle swapped, e.g. clean with microwave), C3 cross-type token-matched placebo, both S=6; C4 self-written same-type short (<= median length) and C5 self-written same-type long-detour (>= 2x median navigation steps), both S=10; class nets against the shared REMOVE-1 without-arm are secondary. E4 cross-fitted deployment: item values (residual + procedural, James-Stein-shrunk toward the class mean with weights from contrast count, pre-registered) averaged over an item's fold-1 retrievals pick the top 3 of the top-10 similarity candidates for fold-2 games, cross-fitted in both directions so every game is deployed once per seed; arms at S=10 (2,740): under B: A-values, B-values, random-3 (similarity top-3 = the natural k=3 arm); under A: A-values, B-values (similarity top-3 = the natural k=3 arm); all arms of a reader are paired game by game. E5 readers C and D: k0, k1, k3, static3, static3+k3, static3+REMOVE 1/2/3 at S=4 (8,768 each), giving their residuals on the same items, split-half rho_CC and rho_DD, the k=1 second composition, and C's k=0 manipulation check. Budget (episodes): A 30,688 (E1 9,316 including top-ups of k0/k1/k3/static3; E2 7,124; E3 8,768; E4 5,480); B 36,716 (E0/E1 12,056; E2 7,672; E3 8,768; E4 8,220); C 8,768; D 8,768; total 84,940. Wall: A at ~10 episodes/min on one replica = 51 h on GPU0; B at ~25/min = 24.5 h, then D and C at ~10/min = 14.6 h each on GPU1 (53.7 h); ~2.2 days with both GPUs busy, ~2.5 days with restarts; the earlier plan's cross-family 8B reader and the E1 arms of C/D were cut to pay for the larger E3/E4 cells. One vLLM replica per GPU, workers raised until each replica's running queue is >= 8. Order: E0-E2 on both GPUs first, then E3, E4 (needs E2's values), then E5. Thresholds pre-registered before E1.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 and static3 arms per reader (procedural credit subtracted before any item claim); token-matched REPLACE vs REMOVE (content vs length); k=1 vs k=3 REMOVE (set composition) and pairwise vs single removal (additivity) under A and B, k=1 vs k=3 under C and D; item-order shuffle control on 1 seed; reader design as a factorial on family, capability and policy: A vs B (same family, weaker), A vs D (other family, capability-matched), A vs C (same backbone, self-distilled policy, valid only if C's k=0 success differs from A's by >= 5 net), so family distance, capability and policy shift are separated; the A split-half correlation is the ceiling every cross-reader correlation is disattenuated against; for E4, in-reader cross-fitted selection is the upper bound, random-3 from the top-10 candidates the floor, similarity top-3 (the natural k=3 arm) the reference, and unshrunk ranking is the ablation of the pre-registered James-Stein shrinkage; subsampling curves (rank correlation between estimates from n and from all contrasts) report the re-runs needed for a stable per-item rank against the LOO baseline cost of one re-run per item per episode.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (class-level transfer, positive control): under both A and B the with-arms at position 1 of the same k=3 set order as C2 planted wrong-procedure < C3 placebo < C1 natural same-type expert, and the direct paired C1 minus C2 contrast is >= +10 net in each reader. C1 and C2 are with-arms on the same (game, seed), so C1-C2 is one paired contrast at 1,644 episodes (+/-4.6), not a difference of two cells, and the +/-5 equivalence band exceeds its CI. Falsified under B if C1-C2 is <= +5 (its CI then excludes +10) or if C2 >= C3 (a planted wrong procedure costs nothing more than a placebo); produced by the E3 arms under B, which run whatever the E0 k-sweep shows, so a weaker reader that ignores item content is a recorded outcome, not a screened one; not entailed, since E0 no longer selects B for consuming items. P2 (residual non-transfer, headline): the disattenuated cross-reader Spearman of item residuals, rho_AB / sqrt(rho_AA rho_BB), is < 0.5 while the within-reader split-half reliabilities rho_AA and rho_BB (seeds 1-3 vs 4-6) are >= 0.5; the aggregate residual under A is the measured +17.2 over static3, and the claim is about its per-item composition, not its magnitude. Falsified if the disattenuated rho_AB is >= 0.8 (residuals transfer: the static3 subtraction left a shared type-level component in the residual) or if rho_AA or rho_BB is < 0.3 (residuals are estimator noise, so there is no item-specific value to transfer); produced by the E2 static3+REMOVE arms under A and B on the same items. The ratio's 95% CI by item bootstrap is about +/-0.25 at 200 items with reliabilities near 0.5, so a point estimate at the predicted 0.5 excludes 0.8 and one at 0.8 excludes 0.5. P3 (where the residual lives): the direct paired C5 long-detour minus C4 short self-written contrast (both with-arms at position 1 on the same (game, seed), 2,740 episodes per arm, +/-3.6) is <= -8 net under B and >= -2 under A, and the reader difference B minus A (game-level bootstrap over the same games; +/-5.1 if treated as independent) is <= -6. Falsified if B's C5-C4 is >= -3 (long detours do not hurt the weaker reader), if A's is <= -7 (they hurt the stronger reader as much), or if B minus A is >= 0 (its CI then excludes -6); produced by the E3 C4/C5 arms under both readers. Secondary: per-item residual_B minus residual_A of self-written items with >= 8 contrasts under both readers regressed on trajectory length. P4 (deployment): under B, paired game by game on the same fold-2 (game, seed) at 2,740 episodes per arm (+/-3.6): B-values minus A-values >= +6 net, B-values minus similarity top-3 >= +8, A-values minus similarity top-3 <= +2. Falsified if B-values minus A-values is <= +2 (values transfer operationally; the CI excludes +6), or if B-values minus similarity is <= +2 (in-reader estimates are unusable: a winner's-curse outcome, or non-consumption by B, which the E0 arm separates); produced by the E4 arms under B with the pre-registered shrinkage; the mirror under A (A-values minus B-values >= +6) is the secondary symmetric test. P5 (policy shift vs backbone swap): disattenuated rho_AC (self-distilled Qwen3-32B) is >= 0.8 and disattenuated rho_AD (gemma-3-27b-it, capability-matched, other family) is < 0.5, both against the same A split-half ceiling and with item-bootstrap CIs (about +/-0.25); the C half is valid only if C's k=0 success differs from A's by >= 5 net (the manipulation check that the policy moved), otherwise it is reported as untested. Falsified if rho_AC is < 0.5 with rho_CC >= 0.5 (a policy shift alone re-ranks the items: the residual is a policy property, the G16 drift outcome), or if rho_AD is >= 0.8 (a capability-matched reader of another family agrees with A, so non-transfer to B was capability, not reader identity); produced by the E5 residual arms under C and D. Not entailed by the shared backbone: reader C is trained on A's own successes with these items in context, so it may have internalized their content, which would collapse (rho_CC < 0.5) or re-rank (rho_AC < 0.5) its residuals, and the prediction is an absolute level against the A ceiling rather than a comparison with rho_AB. P1 is the positive control required before any null in P2-P5 is reported.
Measurement and Noise Control: Every value is a paired contrast on the same (game, seed, retrieved set): net = 100 x (success with minus success without), CIs by game-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) with seed as a blocking factor; cells sized from the measured floor (+/-8 at 548 paired episodes: +/-5.7 at 1,096, +/-4.6 at 1,644, +/-3.6 at 2,740). Class comparisons (P1, P3) and deployment comparisons (P4) are direct paired contrasts between two with-arms on the same (game, seed), whose CI is taken to be no wider than the with/without floor; this is re-estimated from the first two seeds of E3 and cells are topped up if wider, so no prediction rests on a difference of two independent cells and no two predictions share a without-baseline. Item-level quantities are reported as distributions, never as individual effects; per-item residuals use items with >= 8 contrasts (expected 150-250 items, >= 12 contrasts each at S=6); transfer is a comparison of correlations computed from the same contrasts per item, disattenuated by split-half reliabilities on the same items, and the CI of the disattenuated ratio itself (not of a raw Spearman) is estimated by item bootstrap with the split-half re-drawn, expected about +/-0.25 at 200 items. Binding reference: k3 minus static3 = +17.2 [+11.9, +22.4] under A (Measurement C); all residuals are net of static3, no prediction assumes that aggregate is null under any reader, and B's, C's and D's k3 minus static3 are reported arms. Additivity by pairwise vs single removal; winner's-curse control in E4 by cross-fitting plus pre-registered James-Stein shrinkage of item estimates toward their class mean weighted by contrast count. Estimator cost is an estimand: subsampling curves give the re-runs per item for a rank correlation of 0.8 with the full estimate, and LLM-call cost is reported per reader. Seeds and vLLM versions pinned; each arm logged as resumable JSONL under nohup with pid files; one replica per GPU, workers raised until each replica's running queue is >= 8 and utilization >= 50%; throughput reported per replica.
Preprint Collision Check: Channel for all queries: the literature command s2cli (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers; every run reported s2=ok hf=ok); WebSearch was not available in this session, so no section text was read. home: 'data valuation transfer across models proxy model data Shapley rank correlation' -> Data Shapley 1904.02868, OddSHAP 2602.01399, do-Shapley 2602.07203, shapiq 2410.01649, joint Shapley 2107.11357: Shapley estimators only, nothing on cross-model transfer of item values. home: 'data valuation model dependence proxy model transfer selection via proxy influence scores small model to large model' -> 2512.24503 (small proxy runs transfer unreliably to full-scale data-recipe decisions), DataDecide 2504.11393, NN-CIFT 2502.09969, BIDS 2501.12147, DataInf 2310.00902: model-dependence of training-data value is documented for pretraining and instruction data; nothing on in-context retrieved items, no decomposition into invariant and consumer-specific parts, no intervention ground truth on fixed retrieved sets. recent (mechanism, last 12 months): 'memory item utility transfer across backbone models experience reuse LLM agent replaced executor' --recent -> CHIME 2609.02074 (2026-09-02, id verified with s2cli paper: credit-aware hierarchical memory evolution with planning/execution banks; aggregate comparisons, no per-item transfer test), ExpGraph 2605.30712 (closest named method: model-agnostic experience reuse across executors, ablated at module level), Harness the Memory 2608.15008, ElasticMem 2605.30690, Anatomy of Agentic Memory 2602.19320: none measures the same items' counterfactual value under two readers. No pre-emption found; CHIME and ExpGraph are the nearest and are positioned in Related Work.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Reader B may consume items weakly; it is no longer screened out, so a null under B is reported together with its E0 k-sweep, and reader D provides a second consumer for the transfer test at matched capability. Items are retrieved for few games, so item-level ranks are noisy; the design compares correlations at matched noise, restricts to items with >= 8 contrasts and reports the CI of the disattenuated ratio, which at about +/-0.25 separates the 0.5 and 0.8 thresholds only when the point estimate is near one of them; a mid-range estimate (0.6-0.7) is reported as indeterminate, and if within-reader reliability is below 0.3 the study degrades to a class-level result. Manufactured classes are constructed, so class effects may not reflect natural bank composition. The paired with-vs-with CI is assumed no wider than the with/without floor and is verified on the first two seeds before the cells are completed. Serving of gemma-3-27b-it under vLLM must be verified before E5 (fallback Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Instruct); reader C depends on the program's self-distillation job and is uninformative if the LoRA does not move the k=0 policy. ALFWorld only; the procedural/residual decomposition may look different in tasks without a type-level procedure. E4 tests selection among 10 similarity candidates, not bank pruning, so pruning conclusions are indirect.
Addresses gap: G17 (transfer of item utility across consumers, isolated per item against LOO ground truth, with family, capability and policy shift separated by readers B, D and C); the reader C arm attacks the policy-improvement case of G16 directly by asking whether item residual ranks survive self-distillation.
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'static3 - k0 = +12.4, k3 - static3 = +17.2 [+11.9, +22.4] under the Qwen3-32B reader' - measured under one reader, so it says nothing about whether the per-item composition of that +17.2 belongs to the items or to Qwen3-32B; this idea measures the same items' residual over static3 under a second, third and fourth reader on identical sets and predicts that the composition re-ranks while the static3 part transfers. Nearest digest card: arxiv:2605.30712 (ExpGraph) shows model-agnosticism by swapping executors and reporting aggregate success with utility-aware ranking on; it never asks whether an individual experience's utility under executor A is its utility under executor B, which this idea isolates and predicts does not transfer beyond the procedure component. Nearest archived idea: memory_item_value_reliability proposed an audit without an intervention arm and with effects below the noise floor; here every value is a paired REMOVE/REPLACE contrast, class claims are direct paired contrasts at +/-4.6 or +/-3.6, and transfer is a correlation comparison at matched noise with a bootstrap CI on the disattenuated ratio.
Changes made: P1: removed the E0 gate that swapped reader B for Qwen3-14B; E0 is a reported k-sweep and E3 runs under B regardless, so the escape (a reader that ignores content) is a recordable outcome; C1-C2 recast as a direct paired with-vs-with contrast at 6 seeds (+/-4.6) so the +/-5 band exceeds the CI and no without-baseline is shared with P3. P2 (headline, kept open): static arm changed to Measurement C's static3 with the +17.2 aggregate named as the binding reference; E2 static3+REMOVE arms raised to 6 seeds (>= 12 contrasts per item); the CI of the disattenuated ratio stated (+/-0.25) and the 0.5/0.8 thresholds shown to exclude each other at that noise. P3: C4/C5 raised to 10 seeds (2,740, +/-3.6) as direct paired contrasts; the reader difference given its own CI (+/-5.1) with a predicted -6 against a falsifying 0; per-item paired B-minus-A regression added as secondary. P4: E4 arms raised to 2,740 paired episodes with every comparison a game-by-game paired contrast (+/-3.6); thresholds moved to +6/+8 vs +2 so each falsifier is separable; James-Stein shrinkage pre-registered for the winner's curse; A-side cells cut to two. P5: replaced the rho_AC vs rho_AB comparison (entailed by the shared backbone) with absolute levels against the A split-half ceiling, added the capability-matched cross-family reader D (gemma-3-27b-it) in place of Llama-3.1-8B, added a manipulation check that C's policy moved, and stated the ratio CI. Budget: C/D reduced to the E2 core plus k1; 84,940 episodes, ~2.2 days wall with both GPUs busy, arithmetic stated per reader. Sharpness kept: the central claim was strengthened rather than hedged by adding the backbone-not-policy prediction and by moving every threshold onto a paired contrast where the falsifier is reachable, instead of widening the bands or dropping the transfer claim.
